beats.intro: A table is a tidy way to keep track of equivalent ratios. [[q]]Once you know one row, you can fill in the rest.
beats.unitRow: A runner's coach records her laps and minutes. [[r1]]Three laps take nine minutes. [[r2]]Six laps take eighteen minutes. [[q]]How long does one lap take? [[div]]Divide the minutes by the laps: nine divided by three is three. [[check]]And eighteen divided by six is also three. [[fill]]So one lap takes three minutes. That's the unit rate, and it goes in the first row. [[more]]With the unit rate, any row is easy: ten laps take ten times three, which is thirty minutes.
beats.scale: You can also move between rows without the unit rate. [[q]]Going from three laps to six laps doubles the laps, [[x2]]so the minutes double too: nine becomes eighteen. [[rule]]Whatever you multiply one column by, you multiply the other column by the same number. That's what makes a table proportional.
beats.compare: Tables make comparisons easy. [[q]]Two runners, Ann and Hiro, have their own tables. [[ann]]Ann runs three laps in twelve minutes: that's four minutes per lap. [[hiro]]Hiro runs two laps in ten minutes: that's five minutes per lap. [[who]]Ann needs less time for each lap, so Ann is faster. [[warn]]Be careful: fewer minutes per lap means faster, not slower.
beats.notProp: Not every table is proportional. [[q]]Here's a taxi fare: a three-dollar starting fee plus two dollars per kilometer. [[rows]]One kilometer costs five dollars. Two kilometers cost seven. Four kilometers cost eleven. [[test]]Divide each cost by the distance: five, three and a half, and two point seven five. [[no]]The ratios are not all the same, so this table is not proportional. [[why]]Doubling the distance does not double the cost, because of the starting fee. [[rule]]Only use unit rates and scaling when every row has the same ratio.
beats.wrap: In a proportional table, [[w1]]every row has the same ratio: the unit rate. [[w2]]Find it by dividing, and write it in the one-unit row. [[w3]]Fill other rows by multiplying the unit rate, or by scaling both columns by the same number. [[w4]]If the ratios differ from row to row, the table isn't proportional. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final2: Next, decide whether each table is proportional.
beats.final3: Last one. Decide whether each statement is true or false.
